```{r paths}
merged_path <- file.path("output", "02_Integration_clustering", "merged_hippocampus_clustered.rds")
ref_path    <- "/home/vkorob/Documents/data_scripts/RNA_seq/10x_scRNAseq_jessberger/Final_Annotation.rds"

out_dir   <- file.path("output", "03a_RCTD_spotdeconvolution")

dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

max_cores <- 2
eval_RCTD = TRUE    # TRUE = run RCTD and save results; FALSE = load the saved results below

if (!eval_RCTD) {
  weights_all  <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "rctd_weights_GC_ML.csv"))
  rctd_results <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "rctd_results_GC_ML.rds"))
}
```

## Load merged spatial object and reference

```{r load-data}
merged_obj <- readRDS(merged_path)
ref_seurat <- readRDS(ref_path)

table(merged_obj$region)
table(merged_obj$sample)
```

## Build the full scRNA-seq reference
```{r build-full-reference, eval=eval_RCTD}
ref_counts <- GetAssayData(ref_seurat, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")

# Create a new merged column
ref_seurat$Celltype_updated <- ref_seurat$Celltype %>%
  gsub("qNSC|nIPC|Neuroblast","Neurogenic_lineage",. ) %>%
  gsub("SMC|Pericyte|Endothelial","Vascular",. ) %>%
  gsub("Cajal-Retzius","Cajal.Retzius",. )   # syntactic name: survives read.csv() and formulas

cell_types <- ref_seurat$Celltype_updated
names(cell_types) <- colnames(ref_seurat)
cell_types <- as.factor(cell_types)

table(cell_types)
```

## Define which cell types are candidates in each region

```{r region-celltypes}
region_celltypes <- list(
  DG = c("GC", "Neurogenic_lineage", "Astrocyte", "Microglia", "Vascular", "OPC"),
  ML = c("Astrocyte", "Microglia", "Vascular", "OPC", "Cajal.Retzius")
)

region_celltypes
```

## Build one RCTD reference per region (built once, reused across all samples)

```{r build-region-references, eval=eval_RCTD}
region_references <- map(region_celltypes, build_region_reference,
                          ref_counts = ref_counts, cell_types = cell_types)
```

## Loop over every sample x region combination

`run_rctd_region()` (in helper_functions.R) runs RCTD on one sample x region subset.

```{r run-all, eval=eval_RCTD, results="hide"}
sample_names <- unique(merged_obj$sample)
regions_to_run <- names(region_celltypes)   # "DG", "ML"

rctd_results <- list()

for (sample_name in sample_names) {
  for (region_name in regions_to_run) {

    key <- paste(sample_name, region_name, sep = "_")
    message("Running RCTD: ", key)

    sp_sub <- subset(merged_obj, subset = sample == sample_name & region == region_name)

    if (ncol(sp_sub) < 10) {
      warning(key, ": fewer than 10 spots, skipping")
      next
    }

    myRCTD <- run_rctd_region(sp_sub, region_references[[region_name]], max_cores = max_cores)

    rctd_results[[key]] <- list(
      sample   = sample_name,
      region   = region_name,
      rctd_obj = myRCTD
    )
  }
}
```

## Extract and combine weights across all sample x region runs

```{r extract-weights, eval=eval_RCTD}
weights_list <- map(rctd_results, function(res) {

  raw_weights  <- res$rctd_obj@results$weights
  norm_weights <- normalize_weights(raw_weights)

  df <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(norm_weights))
  df$barcode <- rownames(df)
  df$sample  <- res$sample
  df$region  <- res$region
  df$age     <- unique(merged_obj$age[merged_obj$sample == res$sample])

  df
})

weights_all <- bind_rows(weights_list)

write.csv(weights_all, file.path(out_dir, "rctd_weights_GC_ML.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

head(weights_all)
```

## Save the RCTD result objects

```{r save-rctd-objects, eval=eval_RCTD}
saveRDS(rctd_results, file.path(out_dir, "rctd_results_GC_ML.rds"))
```

```{r summary, eval=eval_RCTD}
summary_table
```


# Spearman correlation of markers and RCTD weights

## Positive control markers

```{r QC_markers, warning=FALSE}
validation_markers <- c(
  Astrocyte = "Gfap",
  Microglia = "Aif1",    # Iba1
  GC        = "Prox1",
  Vascular  = "Pdgfrb",
  OPC       = "Pdgfra"
)

DefaultAssay(merged_obj) <- "SCT"

celltype_cols <- setdiff(colnames(weights_all), c("barcode", "sample", "region", "age"))

for (s in plot_samples) {
  sp_sub <- get_sample_with_weights(s, merged_obj, weights_all, celltype_cols)

  for (ct in names(validation_markers)) {
    if (!(ct %in% celltype_cols) || !(validation_markers[[ct]] %in% rownames(sp_sub))) next

    p_weight <- SpatialFeaturePlot(sp_sub, features = ct) + ggtitle(paste0(ct, " (RCTD weight)"))
    p_marker <- SpatialFeaturePlot(sp_sub, features = validation_markers[[ct]]) +

}
```

```{r QC_spearmancorrelation}

colnames(marker_expr) <- names(validation_markers)

correlation_results <- purrr::map_dfr(intersect(names(validation_markers), celltype_cols), function(ct) {
  spearman_cor(validation_df[[paste0(ct, "_weight")]], validation_df[[paste0(ct, "_marker")]]) %>%

correlation_results
```

## Negative control markers
```{r neg_control, warning=FALSE}
negative_control_markers <- c(
  Astrocyte = "Prox1", 
  Microglia = "Prox1",
  GC        = "Gfap", 
  Vascular  = "Gfap",
  OPC       = "Aif1" 
)

housekeeping_gene <- "Actb"  # expressed broadly - not expected in any single cell type specifically

all_genes <- unique(c(validation_markers, negative_control_markers, housekeeping_gene))
all_genes <- intersect(all_genes, rownames(merged_obj))

marker_expr_full <- FetchData(merged_obj, vars = all_genes)
marker_expr_full$barcode <- rownames(marker_expr_full)

correlation_comparison <- purrr::map_dfr(names(validation_markers), function(ct) {

  if (!(ct %in% celltype_cols)) return(NULL)

  weight_vec <- weights_all[[ct]]
  barcode_vec <- weights_all$barcode

  df <- tibble(barcode = barcode_vec, weight = weight_vec) %>%
    left_join(marker_expr_full, by = "barcode")

  real_marker <- validation_markers[[ct]]
  neg_marker  <- negative_control_markers[[ct]]

  real_test <- if (real_marker %in% colnames(df)) spearman_cor(df$weight, df[[real_marker]])
  neg_test  <- if (!is.na(neg_marker) && neg_marker %in% colnames(df)) spearman_cor(df$weight, df[[neg_marker]])
  hk_test   <- if (housekeeping_gene %in% colnames(df)) spearman_cor(df$weight, df[[housekeeping_gene]])

  tibble(
    cell_type             = ct,
    real_marker           = real_marker,
    real_marker_rho       = if (!is.null(real_test)) real_test$rho else NA,
    real_marker_p         = if (!is.null(real_test)) real_test$p_value else NA,
    negative_control      = neg_marker,
    negative_control_rho  = if (!is.null(neg_test)) neg_test$rho else NA,
    negative_control_p    = if (!is.null(neg_test)) neg_test$p_value else NA,
    housekeeping_rho       = if (!is.null(hk_test)) hk_test$rho else NA
  )
})

correlation_comparison
```

```{r neg_control_side, warning=FALSE}
for (ct in names(validation_markers)) {

  if (!(ct %in% celltype_cols)) next

  df <- tibble(barcode = weights_all$barcode, weight = weights_all[[ct]]) %>%
    left_join(marker_expr_full, by = "barcode")

  real_marker <- validation_markers[[ct]]
  neg_marker  <- negative_control_markers[[ct]]

  p_real <- ggplot(df, aes(x = weight, y = .data[[real_marker]])) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "darkgreen") +

    theme_minimal()

  p_neg <- ggplot(df, aes(x = weight, y = .data[[neg_marker]])) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5) +

    labs(title = paste0(ct, " weight vs ", neg_marker, " (negative control)"), x = "RCTD weight", y = "Expression") +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p_real | p_neg)
}
```

# Cajal.Retzius weight validation: combined CR marker score

Cajal.Retzius cells are rare in the adult brain, so any single marker gene can be too sparsely
detected in a Visium spot to give a reliable read on its own -- `Trp73` in particular is only
detected in a handful of ML spots when checked individually. Rather than validate the RCTD
Cajal.Retzius weight against one marker at a time, we combine several canonical CR markers
into a single score, which should be more robust.

`Seurat::AddModuleScore()` is used here: it bins
all genes by their background expression level and subtracts a matched control-gene-set score per
spot, which keeps a comparatively highly-expressed marker (e.g. `Reln`) from dominating the score
and corrects for spot-to-spot differences in overall depth/complexity -- useful here since the
panel mixes a very sparsely-detected gene (`Trp73`) with more commonly detected ones (`Reln`,
`Ndnf`, `Cxcl12`).

```{r cr-marker-score, warning=FALSE}
cr_markers <- c("Reln", "Trp73", "Lhx1", "Ndnf", "Cxcl12")

cr_markers_present <- intersect(cr_markers, rownames(merged_obj))
cr_markers_missing <- setdiff(cr_markers, cr_markers_present)
if (length(cr_markers_missing) > 0) {
  message("CR markers not found in the Visium gene panel (skipped): ",
          paste(cr_markers_missing, collapse = ", "))
}

DefaultAssay(merged_obj) <- "SCT"
merged_obj <- AddModuleScore(merged_obj, features = list(cr_markers_present),
                              name = "CR_score", assay = "SCT")
# AddModuleScore appends a trailing "1" to the name it's given
merged_obj$CR_score <- merged_obj$CR_score1

cr_score_df <- tibble(barcode = colnames(merged_obj), CR_score = merged_obj$CR_score)
nUMI_df_cr  <- tibble(barcode = colnames(merged_obj), nUMI = merged_obj$nCount_Spatial)

ml_cr_df <- weights_all %>%
  filter(region == "ML") %>%
  dplyr::select(barcode, age, Cajal.Retzius) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(Cajal.Retzius) %>%
  left_join(cr_score_df, by = "barcode") %>%
  left_join(nUMI_df_cr, by = "barcode")

cat("ML spots with a Cajal.Retzius weight:", nrow(ml_cr_df), "\n")
```

### Individual markers, for comparison

The same Spearman check as the "Positive control markers" section above, run per CR marker
individually, so the combined score's performance can be judged against each gene on its own.

```{r cr-marker-score-individual, warning=FALSE}
individual_cr_cor <- purrr::map_dfr(cr_markers_present, function(g) {
  expr_vec <- FetchData(merged_obj, vars = g)[ml_cr_df$barcode, 1]
  pct_detected <- mean(expr_vec > 0) * 100
  spearman_cor(ml_cr_df$Cajal.Retzius, expr_vec) %>%
    mutate(marker = g, pct_spots_detected = pct_detected, .before = 1)
})

individual_cr_cor
```

### Combined score vs. RCTD weight

**We obtain negative correlation, so most likely the CR cells signal is not real**

```{r cr-marker-score-cor, warning=FALSE}
cr_score_cor <- spearman_cor(ml_cr_df$Cajal.Retzius, ml_cr_df$CR_score)
cr_score_cor

# partial correlation controlling for nUMI, same convention used throughout this script
resid_weight  <- resid(lm(Cajal.Retzius ~ nUMI, data = ml_cr_df))
resid_score   <- resid(lm(CR_score ~ nUMI, data = ml_cr_df))
cr_score_pcor <- cor.test(resid_weight, resid_score, method = "pearson")
cr_score_pcor
```

```{r cr-marker-score-plots, warning=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
p_scatter <- ggplot(ml_cr_df, aes(x = Cajal.Retzius, y = CR_score, color = age)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = AGE_COLORS) +
  labs(x = "RCTD Cajal.Retzius weight (ML spots)", y = "Combined CR marker score",
       title = paste0("Combined CR score vs. RCTD weight (rho = ", round(cr_score_cor$rho, 3),
                       ", p = ", signif(cr_score_cor$p_value, 2), ")")) +
  theme_minimal()

ml_cr_df <- ml_cr_df %>%
  mutate(cr_quartile = ntile(Cajal.Retzius, 4),
         cr_quartile = factor(cr_quartile, labels = c("Q1 (lowest)", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 (highest)")))

quartile_summary <- ml_cr_df %>%
  group_by(cr_quartile) %>%
  summarise(mean_score = mean(CR_score), se = sd(CR_score) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

p_quartile <- ggplot(quartile_summary, aes(x = cr_quartile, y = mean_score)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_score - se, ymax = mean_score + se), width = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "RCTD Cajal.Retzius weight (quartile)", y = "Mean combined CR score",
       title = "Combined CR score by CR-weight quartile (flat = no tracking)") +
  theme_minimal()

p_scatter | p_quartile
```

```{r marker_celltype_heatmap, warning=FALSE}
nUMI_df <- tibble(

marker_cols <- c(unname(validation_markers), housekeeping_gene)

compute_ct_marker_cor <- function(df, celltype_cols, marker_cols) {
  expand_grid(cell_type = celltype_cols, marker = c(marker_cols, "nUMI")) %>%
    mutate(rho = map2_dbl(cell_type, marker,
                          ~ cor(df[[.x]], df[[.y]], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
}

full_ct_marker_cor <- diag_df %>%
  group_by(age) %>%
  group_modify(~ compute_ct_marker_cor(.x, celltype_cols, marker_cols)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(age = factor(age, levels = c("young", "middle", "old")))

ggplot(full_ct_marker_cor, aes(x = marker, y = cell_type, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "white", high = "darkgreen", midpoint = 0) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(rho, 2)), size = 3) +

  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

# Check correlation between every celltype using weight permutation approach

RCTD weights sum to 1 per spot, so raw correlations between cell type proportions are biased: an increase in one weight forces a decrease elsewhere. We correct for this with a centered log-ratio (CLR) transform, which re-computes each cell type's weight relative to that spot's own geometric-mean weight rather than a fixed total, making standard correlation valid. Because CLR transforms of a fixed composition still carry a residual, structural correlation bias even under true independence, we build an empirical null: for each cell type, weights are shuffled across spots independently (breaking real pairing while preserving that type's own distribution), and the CLR + correlation is recomputed, repeated 500 times. The z-score for each cell type pair is (observed correlation − mean of permuted correlations) / SD of permuted correlations — how many standard deviations the true colocalization signal sits above what pure chance and compositional structure alone would produce.

```{r coloc-zscore, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(1)
coloc_DG <- analyze_coloc_for_region(weights_all, "DG", region_celltypes)
coloc_ML <- analyze_coloc_for_region(weights_all, "ML", region_celltypes)

z_all <- bind_rows(
  make_z_df(coloc_DG, "DG"),
  make_z_df(coloc_ML, "ML")
)

ggplot(z_all, aes(x = ct1, y = ct2, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(z, 1)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "white", high = "darkgreen", midpoint = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~region, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Cell type colocalization (permutation z-score), by region", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

# Check partial correlation accounting for other celltypes

Two cell types can appear correlated not because they directly colocalize, but because both independently correlate with a third factor. Partial correlation isolates the direct relationship between two cell types by statistically removing the variance they each share with all other cell types in the composition, leaving only the association specific to that pair.

How the Calculation Works:
Partial correlation relies on linear regression and the analysis of unexplained variance (residuals):
- Predict Variable X: You run a linear regression predicting your first main variable (X) using the control variable (Z), and find the leftover piece or residual (\(e_{x}\)).
- Predict Variable Y: You run another linear regression predicting your second main variable (Y) using the same control variable (Z), and find its residual (\(e_{y}\)).
- Correlate the Residuals: You compute the standard correlation between the two sets of residuals (\(e_{x}\) and \(e_{y}\)). This final value represents what is left of the relationship between X and Y after stripping away the shared impact of Z

**Example: computing correlation between OPC and CR celltypes:**

```r
resid_OPC <- resid(lm(OPC ~ Astrocyte + Microglia + Vascular, data = ml_df))
resid_CR  <- resid(lm(Cajal.Retzius ~ Astrocyte + Microglia + Vascular, data = ml_df))

cor(resid_OPC, resid_CR)
```

`compute_pcor_region()` and `make_pcor_df()` live in helper_functions.R.

```{r partial-cor, warning=FALSE}
pcor_DG <- compute_pcor_region(weights_all, "DG", region_celltypes)
pcor_ML <- compute_pcor_region(weights_all, "ML", region_celltypes)

pcor_all <- bind_rows(
  make_pcor_df(pcor_DG, "DG"),
  make_pcor_df(pcor_ML, "ML")
)

ggplot(pcor_all, aes(x = ct1, y = ct2, fill = estimate)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(estimate, 2), "\n", sig)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "white", high = "darkgreen", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~region, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Cell type colocalization (partial correlation, controlling for other types), by region",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```


# Build the ligand-receptor resource (mouse orthologs)

```{r lr-resource, warning=FALSE}
op_resource <- select_resource("Consensus")[[1]]

# convert human genes from liana to mouse
orth_source <- orthologs(genes = op_resource$source_genesymbol, species = "mouse", human = TRUE)
orth_target <- orthologs(genes = op_resource$target_genesymbol, species = "mouse", human = TRUE)

source_map <- orth_source %>%
  transmute(human = human_symbol, mouse = symbol) %>%
  filter(!is.na(human), !is.na(mouse)) %>%
  distinct(human, .keep_all = TRUE)

target_map <- orth_target %>%
  transmute(human = human_symbol, mouse = symbol) %>%
  filter(!is.na(human), !is.na(mouse)) %>%
  distinct(human, .keep_all = TRUE)

lr_resource_mouse <- op_resource %>%
  inner_join(source_map, by = c("source_genesymbol" = "human")) %>%
  rename(source_mouse = mouse) %>%
  inner_join(target_map, by = c("target_genesymbol" = "human")) %>%
  rename(target_mouse = mouse) %>%
  # keep both original human symbols (for reference) and the mouse symbols to actually use downstream
  distinct(source_mouse, target_mouse, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!grepl("_", source_mouse), !grepl("_", target_mouse))  # drop complexes

norm_expr <- GetAssayData(merged_obj, assay = "SCT", layer = "data")

spot_ids  <- weights_all$barcode
expr_sub  <- norm_expr[, spot_ids]

lr_resource <- lr_resource_mouse %>%
  transmute(source_genesymbol = source_mouse, target_genesymbol = target_mouse) %>%
  filter(source_genesymbol %in% rownames(norm_expr),
         target_genesymbol %in% rownames(norm_expr))

# common depth / age vectors, shared across every cell-type-pair analysis below
nUMI_full <- merged_obj$nCount_Spatial[colnames(expr_sub)]

age_map_full  <- setNames(weights_all$age, weights_all$barcode)
age_vec_full  <- age_map_full[colnames(expr_sub)]
```

# Ligand-receptor signaling vs cell-type colocalization

For each pair of cell types below, we ask two related questions:

1. Which ligand-receptor pairs' same-spot co-expression tracks how strongly that pair of cell types colocalizes (`coloc_strength` = product of their RCTD weights), after adjusting for sequencing depth (nUMI)?
2. Does that relationship change across age (young / middle / old)?

`run_lr_coloc_pipeline()` (helper_functions.R) does all of this in one call for a given `(ct1, ct2)` pair: it builds `coloc_strength`, restricts to spots where both cell types have valid RCTD candidates (this matters for OPC-Cajal.Retzius below, since Cajal.Retzius is only a candidate in the ML region), then runs the:

1. same-spot correlation
2. the coloc-tracking correlation
3. the age-interaction model
4. the age-stratified detection-enrichment analysis. 

The plotting helpers below (`plot_top_lr_bar`, `plot_lr_volcano`, `plot_lr_vs_coloc_scatter`, `plot_quadrant_scatter`, `plot_metric_trajectory`) are shared across all four pairs.

## Astrocyte - Vascular

```{r lr-pipeline-astro-vasc, warning=FALSE}
astro_vasc <- run_lr_coloc_pipeline(weights_all, expr_sub, lr_resource,
                                     ct1 = "Astrocyte", ct2 = "Vascular",
                                     nUMI_vec = nUMI_full, age_vec = age_vec_full)

astro_vasc$n_spots_used
```

```{r plots-astro-vasc, warning=FALSE, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
plot_top_lr_bar(astro_vasc$lr_vs_coloc, astro_vasc$pair_label)

plot_lr_volcano(astro_vasc$lr_vs_coloc, astro_vasc$pair_label)

# example: the single strongest hit
top_hit <- astro_vasc$lr_vs_coloc %>% filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>% slice_max(abs(rho_vs_coloc), n = 1)
plot_lr_vs_coloc_scatter(top_hit$source_genesymbol, top_hit$target_genesymbol,
                          astro_vasc$expr_sub, astro_vasc$coloc_strength, astro_vasc$lr_vs_coloc,
                          astro_vasc$pair_label)

plot_quadrant_scatter(astro_vasc$same_spot_vs_coloc, x = "rho_same_spot", y = "rho_vs_coloc",
                       sig_col = "both_sig", quad_labels = make_same_spot_quad_labels(),
                       xlab = "Same-spot ligand-receptor co-expression (partial rho, adj. for nUMI)",
                       ylab = paste0("LR product vs ", astro_vasc$pair_label, " coloc strength (partial rho, adj. for nUMI)"),
                       title = paste0("LR pairs co-expressed and tracking ", astro_vasc$pair_label, " colocalization"))

plot_quadrant_scatter(astro_vasc$age_model, x = "slope_young", y = "slope_old",
                       sig_col = "sig_old", quad_labels = make_age_shift_quad_labels(), diagonal = TRUE,
                       xlab = "Slope (coloc -> LR product), young", ylab = "Slope (coloc -> LR product), old",
                       title = paste0(astro_vasc$pair_label, ": coupling shifts with age"),
                       subtitle = "Off-diagonal = age-dependent change; colored = significant old-vs-young shift (p_adj < 0.05)")

plot_metric_trajectory(build_age_trajectory_df(astro_vasc$age_model),
                        color_map = c(slope = "#0072B2"),
                        title = paste0(astro_vasc$pair_label, ": age trajectory of the 12 largest shifts"))

plot_metric_trajectory(build_combined_shift_trajectory_df(astro_vasc$combined_shift),
                        color_map = c("Coloc -> LR product slope" = "#0072B2", "Detection enrichment" = "#D55E00"),
                        title = paste0(astro_vasc$pair_label, ": slope and detection enrichment moving together across age"))
```

## Gene- and pair-level expression by age

```{r astro-vasc-violins, warning=FALSE, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
genes_of_interest <- c("Ptn", "Sdc4", "Ptprz1", "Apoe", "Lrp1", "Psap", "Gpr37l1", "Gnai2", "S1pr1")

expr_long <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(astro_vasc$expr_sub[genes_of_interest, , drop = FALSE]))) %>%
  rownames_to_column("barcode") %>%
  pivot_longer(-barcode, names_to = "gene", values_to = "expression") %>%
  mutate(age = factor(astro_vasc$age[barcode], levels = c("young", "middle", "old")))

plot_violin_by_age(expr_long, y_col = "expression", facet_col = "gene",
                    title = "Ligand/receptor gene expression by age", y_lab = "SCT-normalized expression")

top_pairs_genes <- astro_vasc$lr_vs_coloc %>%
  filter(p_adj < 0.05, rho_vs_coloc > 0) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = rho_vs_coloc, n = 6) %>%
  dplyr::select(source_genesymbol, target_genesymbol)

lr_product_df <- pmap_dfr(top_pairs_genes, function(source_genesymbol, target_genesymbol) {
  ligand <- source_genesymbol; receptor <- target_genesymbol
  if (!(ligand %in% rownames(astro_vasc$expr_sub)) || !(receptor %in% rownames(astro_vasc$expr_sub))) return(NULL)
  tibble(barcode = colnames(astro_vasc$expr_sub),
         pair = paste0(ligand, "-", receptor),
         lr_product = astro_vasc$expr_sub[ligand, ] * astro_vasc$expr_sub[receptor, ],
         age = factor(astro_vasc$age[colnames(astro_vasc$expr_sub)], levels = c("young", "middle", "old")))
})

plot_violin_by_age(lr_product_df, y_col = "lr_product", facet_col = "pair",
                    title = "Top LR pair activity by age", y_lab = "Ligand x Receptor expression product")
```

# Spatial location of high/low colocalization spots

`classify_coloc_quartile()` labels each spot "High" (top quartile), "Low" (bottom quartile), or "Mid", computed separately within each age group — exactly the same split used by `compute_detection_by_age()`, so what you see here is precisely which spots fed the detection-enrichment numbers above. `plot_coloc_spatial()` draws that classification on tissue for one sample.

```{r spatial-coloc-quartiles, warning=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=10}
for (s in plot_samples) {
  p1 <- plot_coloc_spatial(s, astro_vasc, merged_obj)
  p2 <- plot_coloc_spatial(s, vasc_microglia, merged_obj)
  print(p1 | p2)
}
```

## How much do the two pairs' High/Mid/Low spots overlap?

`compute_coloc_overlap()` cross-tabulates the two pipelines' per-spot classification directly (not just visually) and reports Jaccard overlap for the two cells that matter most: High-High (spots colocalized for both pairs — candidate "shared vascular hub" spots) and Low-Low (excluded from both).

```{r coloc-overlap, warning=FALSE}
overlap_av_vm <- compute_coloc_overlap(astro_vasc, vasc_microglia)

overlap_av_vm$contingency          # raw counts
round(overlap_av_vm$proportions, 3)   # as a fraction of all shared spots
overlap_av_vm$jaccard_high_high
overlap_av_vm$jaccard_low_low
overlap_av_vm$chisq_p              # tiny p-value here mostly just reflects large n — read the Jaccard values, not this, for effect size

plot_coloc_overlap(overlap_av_vm)
```

Worth checking whether the overlap is age-dependent too, since the High/Low thresholds are computed per age:

```{r coloc-overlap-by-age, warning=FALSE}
overlap_av_vm$overlap_df %>%
  count(age, group1, group2) %>%
  group_by(age) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(group1 == "High", group2 == "High")   # High-High overlap rate, by age
```

# Save data for LIANA+ CCC (scRNA-seq), all 4 cell-type pairs

`03b_runLiana_scRNAseq.ipynb` runs the permutation-based CCC test only once per age, using the pooled candidate LR pairs from all 4 spatial pipelines above — then filters that single result into 4 per-pair CSVs (`liana_astro_vasc_by_age.csv`, `liana_vasc_microglia_by_age.csv`, `liana_opc_cr_by_age.csv`, `liana_neuro_gc_by_age.csv`). No need to rerun the permutation step separately per pair.

```{r save-for-liana, warning=FALSE}
export_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "ref_export")   # read by 03b_runLiana_scRNAseq.ipynb
dir.create(export_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

lognorm <- GetAssayData(ref_seurat, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
Matrix::writeMM(as(lognorm, "sparseMatrix"), file.path(export_dir, "lognormalized_matrix.mtx"))
writeLines(rownames(lognorm), file.path(export_dir, "features.tsv"))
writeLines(colnames(lognorm), file.path(export_dir, "barcodes.tsv"))

meta <- ref_seurat@meta.data %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("barcode") %>%
  dplyr::select(barcode, Celltype = Celltype_updated, Age)   # merged labels, same as the RCTD cell types

write.csv(meta, file.path(export_dir, "metadata.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

combined_candidate_resource <- bind_rows(
  astro_vasc$candidate_pairs     %>% mutate(spatial_pair = astro_vasc$pair_label),
  vasc_microglia$candidate_pairs %>% mutate(spatial_pair = vasc_microglia$pair_label),
  opc_cr$candidate_pairs         %>% mutate(spatial_pair = opc_cr$pair_label),
  neuro_gc$candidate_pairs       %>% mutate(spatial_pair = neuro_gc$pair_label)
) %>%
  distinct(source_genesymbol, target_genesymbol, .keep_all = TRUE)

write.csv(combined_candidate_resource %>% dplyr::select(-pair, -spatial_pair) %>%
            rename(ligand = source_genesymbol, receptor = target_genesymbol),   # liana-py's expected column names
          file.path(export_dir, "candidate_resource.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Save the spatial LR-colocalization pipeline results (read by 03c)

`03c_crossModality_plots.qmd` compares these four `run_lr_coloc_pipeline()` results against the LIANA+ output from `03b_runLiana_scRNAseq.ipynb`. Saving them here means 03c doesn't have to reload the Visium object or rerun the pipelines.

```{r save-spatial-pipelines, warning=FALSE}
lr_coloc_pipelines <- list(
  astro_vasc     = astro_vasc,
  vasc_microglia = vasc_microglia,
  opc_cr         = opc_cr,
  neuro_gc       = neuro_gc
)

saveRDS(lr_coloc_pipelines, file.path(out_dir, "lr_coloc_pipelines.rds"))
```
